text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Around 300 Albanians have sued the president of a pyramid scheme operator. He allegedly fled the country with $13 million. Police have arrested four of his staff.
- The annual report of Human Rights Watch said Albania's respect of human rights deteriorated significantly in 1996.
- President Sali Berisha dealt only with the issue of Kosovo problem at an OSCE summit in Lisbon. He did not refer to Albanian friction with the organisation.
- Most opposition parties silent in response to comments by Berisha that parliament may draw up a new constitution.
- Two U.S. counsellors will assist Azem Hajdari, a ruling party MP, who is heading a rival faction of the biggest independent trade union in the country.
- The government will increase its engagement in employment and profesional education, the deputy minister of labour and social affairs said.
- Albania's electric corporation suffers big losses from state-owned companies and individuals that have not paid for power use.
- An increase of money in circulation as people receive big returns from pyramid schemes may have been a cause of a continuous rise in the consumer price index over the last three weeks.
- New Tirana mayor Albert Brojka has carried out a major reshuffle at city hall.
- An unregistered and unrecognized trade union with the same name as the biggest Independent Trade Union, headed by MP Azem Hajdari, called for strikes this month.
- Some opposition leaders expressed their thanks for the United State's criticism of Albania's behaviour regarding elections, a new constitution and the press.
- The miners' trade union says the government should annul a contract with the German Preussag company because it claims Albania sold chromium too cheaply.
- Production by Albania's state-owned heavy industry enterprises in the third quarter of the year was 25 percent less than 1993.
